key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can propose low-energy quantum circuit parameters for structured problems, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters offer independently evaluable candidates, making them more reliable to assess than direct, potentially unphysical energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Optionally refine parameters using iterative energy feedback.
Evaluate random, structured parent, and molecular Hamiltonians, plus blind circuit interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found larger energy errors than Adam on general Hamiltonians, limited gains from feedback, and promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians.
watch_item: Do not assume physical validity of direct minimum-energy predictions: some fell below the Hamiltonian spectral lower bound.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
